processing: Little is published about a house method; as with Chinese black teas generally, the leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Not specifically documented. As in other Chinese black teas, the spring picking is usually the most prized.
appearance_dry: Typical of Chinese black teas of its kind: dark, twisted strips.
taste_profile: Few tasting accounts exist for this tea; a smooth, gently sweet cup is what its class would suggest.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Chinese black tea; lengthen the steeps if the cup seems thin.

vintage_note: As is usual for regional Chinese black tea, it is sold as a current-year product, with the harvest season worth asking about. Drink it within a year or two. No aged market is recorded.
description:
Ziyang Hong is the black tea of Ziyang County in Ankang, southern Shaanxi, and the name is registered as a geographical-indication certification mark. Ziyang is one of China's most northerly old tea districts and is known above all for selenium-rich green tea.

The black version follows the general pattern of withering, rolling, oxidising and drying. Details particular to Ziyang are hard to come by, so don't take any single maker's method as the definition of the tea.

In the cup, expect something in the smooth, gently sweet range typical of Chinese black tea, and check it against the bag in hand, since few independent tasting notes exist. Start with short steeps and adjust.

When buying, look for the Ziyang origin and the harvest season. Selenium is the county's main selling point, but it says nothing about how good a tea tastes.
history: Ziyang has a long reputation for tea, with local accounts that reach back very far and should be read as local tradition. Little is documented about when black tea joined the county's green tea, beyond the fact that Ziyang Hong now carries its own certification mark.
